summary:
I fixed and regression-tested 9 of the 10 findings. For the 10th (#7, top-level scalar responses) the premise was wrong, so I fixed it the way Elasticsearch actually behaves. `cargo clippy -p search-yaml --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean and `cargo test -p search-yaml` is green (91 unit, 4+1 ignored runner, 3 YAML robustness), repeated 6 times plus 40 runs of the HTTP tests, with no failures. All downloaded suites still parse cleanly under the stricter parser: ES free 3685 tests, platinum 3027, OpenSearch 1506, clients-tests 220. I did not rerun the real-ES baseline: that needs a dedicated Elasticsearch container, which this task doesn't allow, and the shared reference cluster can't be wiped. I only used it to capture one real Warning header and to confirm it accepts `charset=UTF-8` bodies.

Per finding:
1. **Lone-quote Warning panic:** confirmed and fixed. Header parsing is rewritten with bounds-checked slicing. Panics are now contained at two levels: a panicking test becomes a failed result (`step: "panic"`) and its connection is dropped; a file-level panic fails that file's tests and the run carries on.
2. **Duplicate keys:** confirmed and fixed. JSON, CBOR, Smile and the YAML parser (test files and YAML responses) now reject a repeated field with Jackson's `Duplicate field 'f'`.
3. **HTTP retry after the request was sent:** confirmed and fixed. The client now uses hyper's `try_send_request` and resends only when hyper hands the request back unsent, or on a reset on a reused keep-alive connection (the idle-close race, where the server never read our bytes). A connection closed after the request went out is now an error.
4. **Capability errors cached as unknown:** confirmed and fixed. `capability()` now matches `checkCapability`: 200 gives the answer, 4xx means unknown, both are cached. 5xx, other statuses, transport errors and a non-boolean `supported` fail the test and are not cached.
5. **Loose Warning-header pattern:** confirmed and fixed. Headers must now match `WARNING_HEADER_PATTERN` exactly: version required, hash of 7 or 40 lowercase hex or `unknown`. OpenSearch uses its own stricter text rules. Value extraction also matches Java now: first quote to last character, so a warn-date stays in the value, and the lazy XContent-location strip is exact.
6. **Stale baseline pass list:** confirmed and fixed. New `run_for_baseline` in the script deletes the report and pass list first, tolerates exit status 1 and aborts on anything higher or when no pass list was written. I tested it with a fake runner.
7. **Scalar JSON responses:** the claim that Elasticsearch rejects them is wrong. `mapOrdered()` → `findNonEmptyMapStart` returns an empty map for a scalar root, so the Java runner reads `true` as `{}` (its `is_true: ''` passes too). Our runner now does the same: arrays and maps are kept, any other root becomes `{}`, and the response text is unchanged.
8. **Missing `charset=UTF-8`:** confirmed and fixed. Bodies and the random `GET ?source_content_type=` now use `<media type>; charset=UTF-8`, as Elasticsearch's runner sends them.
9. **Lax prerequisite validation:** confirmed and fixed. All checks from `PrerequisiteSectionBuilder.validate` now apply, only when a section actually has `skip`/`requires`. String bodies must be JSON: they are parsed the way `DoSection` does (comments allowed, duplicates rejected, non-object tokens read as `{}`), and `Body::Raw` is gone. `transform_and_set` now drops trailing empty parts when splitting on `,`, like Java's `split`.
10. **Regex `.` matched line terminators:** confirmed and fixed. Outside a character class and without `(?s)`, `.` becomes `[^\n\r\x{85}\x{2028}\x{2029}]`.
public_api:
Unchanged except:
- `target::TargetInfo::capability(&self, &mut Client, &CapabilityCheck) -> Result<Option<bool>, String>`. It used to return `Option<bool>`.
- New `pub const target::CAPABILITY_ERROR: &str`.
- `warnings::is_warning_header(header: &str, flavor: Flavor) -> bool`. It used to take an agent string.
- New `http::Client::disconnect(&mut self)`.
- New `xcontent::MediaType::request_content_type(self) -> String`, e.g. `"application/json; charset=UTF-8"`.
- `suite::Body` now has only `Value(Value)`; `Raw` was removed.
- Everything else as documented in the `search-yaml` section of `docs/search/contracts.md`, which now also covers capability-error semantics, charset, the stricter Warning-header pattern, strict parsing and the no-resend rule.
- Script: `es-baseline` and `os-baseline` now fail instead of writing a baseline when a run aborts (exit status 2 or higher, or no pass list written).
done: crates/search-yaml/src/warnings.rs: hand-written matcher for HeaderWarning.WARNING_HEADER_PATTERN (semver + 7/40 hex or unknown; ES value is `.*` minus quote/backslash checked against the qdtext set; OpenSearch uses strict qdtext with an optional RFC 1123 date). Bounds-checked extract_value from the first quote to the last character, plus an exact lazy `^\[.*?]\[-?\d+:-?\d+] ` strip. Tests: header_shape (reviewer's examples, lone quote, empty input), extraction, lone_quote_is_unmatched_not_a_panic, real_header_is_tolerated_legacy_warning (header captured from the reference ES 9.5.5)

crates/search-yaml/src/runner.rs: allocation-free catch_unwind future (pin! + poll_fn) around run_test and around run_file in the worker loop; panics become failed results and the connection is dropped. A capability error gets Phase::Setup. Scalar response roots become {}. Bodies carry charset=UTF-8 (also in source_content_type). transform_and_set split drops trailing empty parts. Tests: panics_become_results, response_bodies (scalar roots, duplicates in JSON and YAML, empty body, text)

crates/search-yaml/src/http.rs: try_send_request; retry only when the request comes back unsent, or on a reset of a reused connection; Client::disconnect. Tests: dropped_response_is_not_retried (fresh connection, server sees exactly 1 request) and dropped_response_on_a_reused_connection_is_not_retried (sees exactly 2)

crates/search-yaml/src/target.rs: capability() returns Result; 200 and 4xx cached, everything else an uncached error. Test server gained 400, 500-then-200 and non-bool answers; the prerequisites test now expects an unreachable capabilities API to be an error

crates/search-yaml/src/value.rs + xcontent.rs (insert_unique) + yaml/parser.rs (KeySet: linear scan for small maps, hash set once a map reaches 32 keys): duplicate fields rejected everywhere with `Duplicate field 'x'`

crates/search-yaml/src/suite.rs: full PrerequisiteSection validation (only when a skip/requires section exists); string bodies parsed as JSON the way DoSection does, with a comment stripper that errors on an unterminated `/*`; Body::Raw removed. Tests: prerequisite_sections_are_validated_like_java, string_bodies_parse_like_the_java_runner
crates/search-yaml/src/regex_java.rs: Java `.` semantics unless (?s). Test: dot_excludes_every_java_line_terminator

tests/runner.rs: new mock APIs badwarn (lone quote + 12-hex hash: fails as unmatched, run completes) and dup (duplicate field: fails). The echo tests check charset=UTF-8. Line assertion now computed from the fixture
scripts/search-yaml-suites.sh: run_for_baseline helper used by both free and clients phases of es-baseline and by os-baseline
src/spawn.rs: deflaked free_ports_are_bindable (another process on the machine could take the port between the check and the re-bind)
remaining: Rerun `scripts/search-yaml-suites.sh es-baseline` and `os-baseline` with dedicated containers (not allowed in this task). That confirms the stricter warning, duplicate, prerequisite and string-body parsing plus charset change nothing on real ES 9.5.5 and OpenSearch 3.9.0. All suite files already parse with zero errors.

Optional fidelity gaps found while fixing, deliberately left stricter than Java: (a) JSON responses with trailing content after the root value fail here, while Jackson ignores the rest; (b) JSON responses with comments fail here, while Elasticsearch's JSON parser allows comments.
A file-level panic (as opposed to a test-level one) during a --cluster-hook run would not DELETE that file's hook cluster. Spawned processes are still killed by Drop.
tests: `cargo test -p search-yaml`: 91 unit, 4 runner integration (+1 ignored helper), 3 YAML robustness, all passing. Repeated 6 times, plus 40 runs of the HTTP tests, with no failures. `cargo clippy -p search-yaml --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. `search-yaml check` with zero parse errors on ES 9.5.5 test/free (702 files, 3685 tests), platinum (500 files, 3027 tests), OpenSearch 3.9.0 (410 files, 1506 tests) and clients-tests (219 files, 220 tests). compatTest had 10 parse errors in this run (none from the new checks; compatTest is not part of the baseline runs). Real-ES baseline not rerun (needs a dedicated container).
notes_for_others: search-es/search-server: the runner now fails any response that repeats a JSON field (`Duplicate field 'x'`) and any Warning header that doesn't match `299 Elasticsearch-<x.y.z>[-…]-<7 or 40 lowercase hex | unknown> "<text>"`. Elasticsearch 9.5.5 sends `299 Elasticsearch-9.5.5-48acba663b09e70b115dd879329141506c377890 "…"`, so roll must emit a semantic version and a 7- or 40-character hash.

search-es: request bodies from the runner now carry `Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8` (and the same for yaml/cbor/smile and vnd types), like the Java runner. Media-type parameters must be accepted.
search-es/search-control: a 5xx or dropped connection on GET /_capabilities now fails the test instead of silently skipping it; answer 4xx only when the API itself is unsupported.

Anyone running the suites: the runner no longer resends a request after the server may have received it, so a search-dev crash or a dropped response now shows up as a failure instead of passing on retry.
